policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV PRO.11.3 renders the clause 'But the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them', which fits either witness equally: qere ישדם and ketiv ושדם are the same verb (שדד) with the same 3mp suffix, differing only in the prefixed letter, and both yield 'shall destroy them'. The initial 'But' is the ASV's usual English marking of antithetical parallelism in Proverbs, not a rendering of a waw, so it cannot be read as evidence for the ketiv's prefixed waw. No ASV note is mapped to this unit and no italicized supply bears on it, so nothing in the English distinguishes the readings; both remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
